Subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance recap & SLO next steps

Thanks again for the demo time today — really appreciate the detailed walkthrough. Quick recap of the performance / SLO items we discussed and a couple of action items to move the MAP forward: 

SLO / performance targets (as discussed):
- 95th pct latency: <= 120 ms for 512-token responses (p50 target: ~30-40 ms)
- Sustained throughput: 50 requests/sec (with expected burst capacity to 200 rps for short windows)
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 6-10, peak 12
- Streaming: required for user-facing flows; chunking should start delivering tokens within ~50ms of generation and subsequent chunks within ~40-60ms
- Fallback behavior: automatic degrade to smaller model variant if latency exceeds 300 ms or during capacity constraints

Attachments: SLO_checklist.xlsx (draft), MAP_FintechCo_v1.pdf (initial mutual action plan)

Next steps / ask from FintechCo:
1) Please confirm or adjust the targets above (latency/throughput/concurrency/streaming).
2) Confirm preferred perf-test window (we can run tests in your timezone but prefer a 2-3 hour slot during low business hours).
3) Procurement: Priya — if you can confirm SOC2 and procurement timeline so we can align the test and contract dates.

Internal: Dev/Vivek — I copied you for sizing notes and to propose recommended infra/setup.

Thanks — happy to set a 30 min follow-up after you confirm targets.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high-level targets, and a few clarifications/questions below: 

- Latency: 95th <= 120 ms for median-length responses (up to 512 tokens) sounds right. Can you also provide p99 estimates from your perf runs for similar model sizes?
- Throughput: 50 rps sustained, burst to 200 rps is appropriate. We need to understand queueing behavior when burst exceeds capacity — what's the expected tail latency if we allow 30s queuing?
- Concurrency: 8-12 is our expected range during peak trading hours.
- Streaming: required. Important detail: our UI expects the first token within 70 ms of send and subsequent chunks every 50-100 ms. If streaming requires different model config, please call that out.
- Fallbacks: yes, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant is OK, but we need a decision criteria matrix in the MAP (e.g., thresholds and which model variant is used).

Procurement: Priya — we're ready to move quickly but need SOC2 Type II and a standard SLSA + Data Processing Addendum. Can you share those docs?

Perf artifacts: can you provide a small perf-log sample and the exact test harness(s) you use? That will help our infra team validate results.

Preferred test window: next Tue/Wed after 22:00 PT.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure, FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance recap & SLO next steps (internal sizing)

Marissa / Vivek — quick internal note on feasibility and recommended config for the targets above: 

- Model & infra: Recommend dedicated pool (Reserved) with 4 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent Ampere/Tesla tier) for steady 50 rps + burst handling. If they need stronger burst headroom, add 1-2 burst GPUs or enable cross-region fallback.
- Quantization: Use int8/4-bit quantized runtime variant for the main serving path to reduce latency and cost; keep float16 variant for higher-quality fallback. We can route by policy.
- Streaming: Our runtime supports chunked streaming. To hit first-token < 70 ms, we should disable large batching for streaming routes and set continuous-batch window to ~5-10 ms for streaming sessions. For non-streaming batch inference (higher throughput) we can use larger windows.
- Batching: Use adaptive batching with a 10 ms max latency target for inference; that gives us good throughput while keeping p95 in range.
- KV cache: Recommend prefix caching for common prompts (saves ~15-30% tokens and latency on repeated flows).
- Metrics to capture in perf run: p50/p95/p99 latency (client-side and server-side), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue depth, and streaming chunk timing (time-to-first-chunk, inter-chunk gaps).

Estimated timeline for a meaningful perf report: 7-10 business days if we schedule a dedicated perf window and get access to test data and sample logs. If they want an accelerated 48-hour smoke test, we can do that but results will be less robust.

Attaching a small perf log sample and our test harness notes.

Thanks,

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick confirm and details. Per Dev's notes (copied below), we've attached an updated SLO checklist and a MAP with the decision criteria matrix and proposed perf plan. Quick summary and next steps: 

Decision criteria (please confirm):
- Accept if p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 300 ms for 512-token responses on the streaming route.
- Accept sustained throughput: 50 rps for 1-hour run with peak bursts to 200 rps for at least 5 minutes without p95 > 300 ms.
- Streaming: time-to-first-token <= 70 ms, inter-chunk <= 100 ms.
- Fallback: automatic to smaller variant when queue depth > X or when p95 > 300 ms for 2 consecutive minutes (we'll state exact thresholds in MAP).

Proposed next steps / owners: 
1) FintechCo: confirm decision criteria above OR provide adjustments (Alex) — by EOD Mon.
2) Redwood: schedule perf window and prepare test harness (Marissa/Dev) — propose Tue 22:00 PT.
3) Procurement: Priya to share SOC2 Type II report and DPA link so Legal can start review.
4) Post-test: Redwood to deliver perf report + recommended Dedicated config and estimated pricing within 3 business days.

Attachments: SLO_checklist.xlsx, MAP_FintechCo_v1.pdf (updated)

Let me know if Tue 22:00 PT works and whether you want us to run the 2-3 hour full test or start with a 1-hour smoke + targeted bursts.
